questions.q: Why does this lesson frame an integration security review as a recurring discipline rather than a one-time, pre-go-live audit?
options: Because configuration drifts over time even when nothing was wrong at launch -- permission sets loosen, certificates near expiry, IP ranges stop matching actual infrastructure
Because Salesforce requires a new review every time a password is reset
Because reviews are only needed if an incident has already occurred
Because integrations automatically fail every 90 days without a review
questions.explain: A review checks whether something already built is still correctly configured, since drift happens on its own over time -- the same logic behind recurring classification review and access recertification elsewhere in governance practice.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is the standard pattern for an inbound webhook or Apex REST endpoint to verify that a request is genuinely from the expected sender?
options: Trusting any request that arrives over HTTPS, since TLS alone proves the sender's identity
Checking only that the request's IP address resolves to a known hostname
Verifying a cryptographic signature (commonly an HMAC over the raw request body) computed with a shared signing key, and rejecting mismatches before business logic runs
No verification is needed if the endpoint is hosted on a Salesforce Site
questions.explain: A public inbound endpoint executes for anyone who finds the URL unless it independently verifies the request -- signature verification against the raw body, checked before any business logic runs, is the standard pattern this lesson describes.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn specifically against computing an HMAC signature over a re-serialized version of the JSON payload instead of the original raw request body?
options: Re-serialization is always faster and therefore always preferred
Re-serialization can change whitespace or key order, which silently breaks a signature check that was actually valid for the original bytes
HMAC verification does not work with JSON payloads at all
Salesforce blocks any Apex code that reads a raw request body
questions.explain: This is flagged as a subtle, common implementation bug: the signature was computed over specific bytes, so checking it against a reconstructed version of the payload can fail even when the original request was perfectly legitimate.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson identify with a webhook endpoint hosted behind a Salesforce Site or Experience Cloud guest user profile, independent of whether signature verification is implemented correctly?
options: Guest user profiles cannot be used for any inbound integration

If the guest user profile has broader object access than the webhook strictly needs, a flaw anywhere in the endpoint's logic executes with that full broader access, not just the webhook's intended data
Guest users automatically bypass all signature verification
There is no additional risk beyond the signature check itself
questions.explain: The same least-privilege discipline from Lesson 6 applies to the guest user profile behind a public endpoint -- over-broad guest user access is a separate risk from signature verification, since the endpoint's code runs with whatever that guest profile can reach.

questions.q: This lesson recommends ranking review findings by risk rather than just listing them. Which pairing reflects the example priority given in the lesson?
options: A slightly stale monitoring baseline outranks a webhook endpoint with no signature verification at all
Only identity-pass findings should ever be prioritized; configuration and monitoring findings can be ignored
All findings should always be treated as equally urgent, regardless of type
A webhook endpoint with no signature verification at all usually outranks a monitoring baseline that's slightly stale
questions.explain: The lesson's example explicitly ranks an unverified public inbound endpoint as higher risk than a merely slightly-stale monitoring baseline -- findings need a specific next action and owner, prioritized by actual risk, not just enumerated.
